![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252107/assets/ad5ee5c0c388e0d2a800765288f20350a8332888a54b4eb3fafd5986d6355838.png)

The line shown above passes through the points $(0,3)$ and $(-2,-1).$ What is the equation of the line?
questions.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b.$ So we need to work out the slope $m$ and the $y$-intercept $b.$

From the graph, we see that the line intercepts the $y$-axis at $(0,3).$ So, the $y$-intercept is $b=3.$

We can calculate the slope of the line by choosing two points on the line and applying the slope formula. The line passes through the points $(0,3)$ and $(-2,-1),$ so we calculate its slope as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}m & =\frac{{y}_{2}-{y}_{1}}{{x}_{2}-{x}_{1}} \\  & =\frac{-1-3}{-2-0} \\  & =\frac{-4}{-2} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the slope $m=2$ and the $y$-intercept $b=3$ into the slope-intercept form $y=mx+b,$ we obtain the equation of the line:

$$
y=2x+3
$$

questions.worked_solution:
We convert the absolute value inequality into a compound inequality to remove the absolute value. 

The inequality specifies every number $12z+7$ whose distance from zero is greater than or equal to $5.$ This corresponds to the following compound inequality:

$$
\begin{aligned}12z+7 & \le -5 & \text{or} &  & 12z+7 & \ge 5\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve each inequality using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}12z+7 & \le -5 &  &  & 12z+7 & \ge 5 \\ 12z & \le -12 &  &  & 12z & \ge -2 \\ z & \le -1 &  &  & z & \ge -\frac{1}{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the final solution is

$$
\begin{aligned}z & \le -1 & \text{or} &  & z & \ge -\frac{1}{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

(-b)+c,

Finally, we use the triangle law to add the vectors $-b$ and $c:$ 

- We can start $-b$ from an arbitrary point on the plane.

- Next, we draw the vector that is equal to $c$ and has its tail placed at the head of $-b.$

- Now, according to the triangle law of addition, the resultant is the vector that goes from the tail of $-\text{b}$ to the head of $\text{c}$, as shown below.

questions.problem:
What is the solution to the following system of inequalities?

$$
\{\begin{aligned}p-2>3 \\ 1-2p\le -7\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve the system, we need to find the values of $p$ that satisfy both $p-2>3$ and $1-2p\le -7$ simultaneously.

- First, we solve $p-2>3\,:$

$$
\begin{aligned}p-2 & >3 \\ p-2+2 & >3+2 \\ p & >5\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252107/assets/1189f49b694afcfef7f10a19b523ebbcce3bb8ab13b69e60ebfd5a6c342ff10e.png)

$$

$$

- Then, we solve $1-2p\le -7\,:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}1-2p & \le -7 \\ 1-2p-1 & \le -7-1 \\ -2p & \le -8 \\ (-1)\cdot (-2p) & \ge (-1)\cdot (-8) \\ 2p & \ge 8 \\ \frac{2p}{2} & \ge \frac{8}{2} \\ p & \ge 4\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252107/assets/f8bf3ae94c8048dcf9060c985300f9a808ae73158eeeef6e0f01f3f922d33ea9.png)

To find the values of $p$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14252107/assets/1a4cd0c86983a39354eef09ad60d44f3815c082f443a3eb12bd14f6232988f65.png)

 

$$

$$

Thus, the final solution is $p\in (5,\infty ).$

questions.problem:
What is $0.9\,\text{g}$ expressed in $\text{mg}?$ Write your answer as a whole number.

$0.9\,\text{g}=$
{{field-1}}$\text{mg}$
questions.worked_solution:
We start by recalling the conversion table for mass units. 

| Name | Symbol | Conversion |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kilogram | $\text{kg}$ | $1\,\text{kg}=1\,000\,\text{g}$ |
| Gram | $\text{g}$ | Base Unit |
| Milligram | $\text{mg}$ | $1\,000\,\text{mg}=1\,\text{g}$ |

$$

$$

There are $1\,000\,\text{mg}$ per $\text{g},$ which we can write as follows:

$$
\frac{1000\,\text{mg}}{\text{g}}
$$

This is our conversion factor.

Now, multiplying $0.9\,\text{g}$ by our conversion factor, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}0.9\,\text{g} & =0.9\,\text{g}\cdot \frac{1\,000\,\text{mg}}{\text{g}} \\  & =0.9\,\cancel{\text{g}}\cdot \frac{1\,000\,\text{mg}}{\cancel{\text{g}}} \\  & =0.9\cdot 1\,000\,\text{mg} \\  & =900\,\text{mg}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $0.9\,\text{g}$ is equivalent to $900\,\text{mg}.$

Given that the triangle $△ABC$ shown above is isosceles, the measure of $\overset{―}{AC}$ must be equal to{{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Since $△ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with base $\overset{―}{AB}$, we have that $\overset{―}{AC}≅\overset{―}{CB}.$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =CB \\ 3x-9 & =2x-1 \\ x & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this value into the expression for the measure of $\overset{―}{AC}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}AC & =3x-9 \\  & =3(8)-9 \\  & =15.\end{aligned}
$$

In the diagram shown above, $B$ is the midpoint of $\overset{―}{AD}.$ Find $BC$ if $AD=29\,\text{cm}$ and $CD=6.5\,\text{cm}.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since $B$ is the midpoint of $\overset{―}{AD}$, we have: 

$$
\begin{aligned}BD & =\frac{1}{2}AD \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 29 \\  & =14.5\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, by the segment addition postulate, we obtain: 

$$
\begin{aligned}BD & =BC+CD \\ 14.5 & =BC+6.5 \\ 14.5-6.5 & =BC \\ BC & =8\,\text{cm}\end{aligned}
$$
